issues.description: Default and tiny extraction point at data/stories, but the repo contains no story files or manifest, so extraction cannot run from source.
Story loading has no fixture fallback or generator despite the README describing a runnable tiny demo.
The advertised end-to-end test fails immediately because its required input dataset is missing.
The demo script is not reproducible from a clean checkout because its first command depends on missing story data.
Documentation claims make demo and equivalent tiny commands run on CPU, but they fail without absent data/stories inputs.
Extraction constructs the backend before validating input data, so the HF path can fail on dependencies/model loading before reporting missing stories.
Manifest writing assumes at least one processed story and crashes with min/max errors for empty or invalid scale settings.
Tiny extraction passes the true emotion label into the backend, making validation less meaningful and potentially masking extraction defects.
TinyResidualBackend directly injects label_hint into activations, creating a self-fulfilling test backend rather than a label-blind approximation.
Validation loads vectors and builds a backend from CLI config without checking manifest backend, model, layer count, or vector dimensionality compatibility.
A custom emotion set with no matching built-in scenarios causes empty-stack or NaN behavior instead of a clear validation error.
Preference steering hard-codes four reported emotions and ignores the configured min_reported_emotions setting.
steering.min_reported_emotions is configured but unused, making the config misleading.
HF dtype='auto' resolves to full default precision and no device_map or low-memory loading, making the documented Gemma run likely to OOM on common machines.
Dependencies are broad lower bounds with no lock file or model revision pin, reducing reproducibility for research outputs.
Checked-in artifacts reference a source story manifest that is not present in the repository, so stored results cannot be regenerated or audited.
